relationships.subject: spinal cord injury
relationships.evidence_quote: This change is linked to the downregulation of the potassium/chloride cotransporter (KCC2)

relationships.subject: KCC2
relationships.evidence_quote: KCC2 is the only Cl− extruder in most CNS neurons

relationships.subject: NKCC1
relationships.evidence_quote: NKCC1, an ion transporter from the NKCC family, is one of the main Cl− intruders.

relationships.subject: spinal microglia
relationships.evidence_quote: inflammatory processes (microglia activation) within the spinal cord, leading to BDNF release and a downregulation in KCC2 in the absence of SCI

relationships.subject: BDNF
relationships.evidence_quote: in the absence of neural injury, the neurotrophin appears to downregulate KCC2 and promote pathological over-excitation

relationships.subject: BDNF
relationships.evidence_quote: BDNF has been shown to up-regulate KCC2 and attenuate both nociceptive sensitization and spasticity after SCI

relationships.subject: ionic plasticity
relationships.evidence_quote: The loss of GABA-dependent inhibition enables a state of over-excitation within the spinal cord that fosters aberrant motor activity (spasticity) and chronic pain.

relationships.subject: benzodiazepines
relationships.evidence_quote: Benzodiazepines bind to sites on the alpha subunits of the GABA-A receptor and act as positive allosteric modulators potentiating the action of endogenous GABA release.

key_findings: Review: SCI and nerve injury downregulate KCC2, raising intracellular Cl- and converting GABA-A signalling from inhibitory to less inhibitory or excitatory (ionic plasticity), which drives spasticity and chronic pain.
BDNF has context-dependent effects on KCC2 (upregulation after SCI, downregulation without injury); KCC2 enhancers such as CLP290 and NKCC1 blockers such as bumetanide are candidate therapies.
